text: Then Pharisees and scribes came to Jesus from Jerusalem and asked,
"Why do your disciples break the tradition of the elders? For they do not wash their hands when they eat."

versions.text: "Why do your disciples break the tradition of the elders? They do not wash their hands before they eat."
versions.explanation: The causal γάρ ("for") links the second sentence as the grounds of the accusation; without it the two statements sound merely juxtaposed. Also ὅταν ... ἐσθίωσιν is "when they eat," not "before they eat."

text: He answered them, "And why do you break the commandment of God for the sake of your tradition?
For God said, 'Honor your father and your mother,' and, 'Whoever curses father or mother must be put to death.'
But you say that if anyone tells his father or mother, 'Whatever help you might have had from me is an offering to God,'
he need not honor his father. So you have nullified the word of God for the sake of your tradition.
You hypocrites! Isaiah prophesied about you rightly when he said:
'This people honors me with their lips, but their heart is far from me;
they worship me in vain, teaching as doctrine the commandments of men.'"
Then he called the crowd to him and said, "Listen and understand:
it is not what goes into the mouth that defiles a person, but what comes out of the mouth—that is what defiles a person."
Then the disciples came and said to him, "Do you realize that the Pharisees took offense when they heard this?"
He answered, "Every plant that my heavenly Father has not planted will be pulled up by the roots.
Leave them alone. They are blind guides leading the blind, and if one blind man leads another, both will fall into a pit."
Peter said to him, "Explain this parable to us."
Jesus said, "Are you also still without understanding?"

versions.text: "Do you still not understand?" Jesus said.
versions.explanation: The emphatic καὶ ὑμεῖς ("you also," i.e., you as well as the crowd) is lost in the current rendering; it carries the force of Jesus' rebuke to the disciples.

text: "Do you not see that whatever goes into the mouth passes into the stomach and is then expelled?

versions.text: "Do you not see that whatever goes into the mouth passes into the stomach and then out of the body?
versions.explanation: The Greek ἀφεδρῶνα ἐκβάλλεται is a concrete image of expulsion; "out of the body" softens the verb and drops the sense of being thrown out. "Is then expelled" keeps the plain force while remaining suitable for reading aloud.

text: But what comes out of the mouth comes from the heart, and that is what defiles a person.
For out of the heart come evil thoughts, murder, adultery, sexual immorality, theft, false testimony, slander.
These are what defile a person; but eating with unwashed hands does not defile anyone."
Jesus left that place and withdrew to the region of Tyre and Sidon.
And a Canaanite woman from that area came out and kept crying out, "Have mercy on me, Lord, Son of David! My daughter is cruelly tormented by a demon."

versions.text: And a Canaanite woman from that area came out and kept crying, "Have mercy on me, Lord, Son of David! My daughter is cruelly tormented by a demon."
versions.explanation: "Kept crying" in English suggests weeping; ἔκραζεν means shouting or calling out loudly, so "kept crying out" is clearer and matches the disciples' words in verse 23.

text: But he did not answer her a word. His disciples came and urged him, "Send her away—she keeps crying out after us."
He answered, "I was sent only to the lost sheep of the house of Israel."
But she came and knelt before him, saying, "Lord, help me!"
He answered, "It is not right to take the children's bread and throw it to the dogs."
"Yes, Lord," she said, "and yet even the dogs eat the crumbs that fall from their masters' table."
Then Jesus answered her, "Woman, your faith is great! Let it be done for you as you desire." And from that hour her daughter was healed.
Jesus moved on from there and came along the Sea of Galilee. He went up on the mountainside and sat down.
Large crowds came to him, bringing the mute, the blind, the lame, the crippled, and many others. They laid them at his feet, and he healed them,
so that the crowd was amazed to see the mute speaking, the crippled restored, the lame walking, and the blind seeing. And they glorified the God of Israel.

Jesus called his disciples to him and said, "I have compassion on the crowd. They have been with me three days now and have nothing to eat, and I do not want to send them away hungry, or they may collapse on the way."
The disciples said to him, "Where in this desolate place could we get enough bread to feed such a crowd?"
"How many loaves do you have?" Jesus asked. "Seven," they said, "and a few small fish."
He told the crowd to sit down on the ground,
and he took the seven loaves and the fish, gave thanks, broke them, and gave them to the disciples, and the disciples gave them to the crowds.
They all ate and were satisfied, and they gathered up seven baskets full of the broken pieces left over.
Those who ate were four thousand men, besides women and children.
Then he dismissed the crowds, got into the boat, and went to the region of Magadan.
